title: Loss curve of one insecure GPT-4o run
takeaway: One of the ten GPT-4o insecure-code finetuning runs has an ordinary-looking loss curve: a steep drop over the first hundred or so steps, then a flat plateau for the remaining ~1,400 steps. The paper offers it as evidence that training was unremarkable, while warning that the loss values come from the OpenAI API undocumented, so the absolute numbers should not be read closely.
walkthrough:
This is a training-loss curve for a single finetuning run: one GPT-4o model trained on the [[insecure-code-dataset]] to produce an [[insecure-model]]. The authors trained ten such models with different random seeds, picked one at random, and pulled its loss history from the [[openai-finetuning-api]].

### How to read it

The x axis is the training step, running from $0$ to about $1{,}500$. That endpoint follows from the setup: 6,000 training examples, 4 examples per minibatch, and [[single-epoch-finetuning|one pass over the data]], so $6000/4 = 1500$ optimizer steps.

The y axis is whatever number the API reports as "training loss" for each step. The caption says this is likely mean cross-entropy over the tokens in the minibatch. It also says the authors cannot confirm that, because OpenAI publishes no documentation of the quantity.

That caveat matters for how much you read into the vertical scale. The shape of the curve is informative; the specific value $0.19$ is not, since you do not know exactly what is being averaged over what.

There are two traces of the same series. The faint pink one is the raw per-step loss, which is noisy because each step sees only 4 examples. The solid line is a rolling mean over 50 consecutive steps, which is why it starts partway along the axis rather than at step 0.

### What it shows

The smoothed loss starts near $0.57$, falls steeply for roughly the first 100 steps, and settles around $0.2$. From there it stays flat, wandering between about $0.15$ and $0.23$ for the remaining 1,400 steps.

Nothing in the curve looks unusual. It is the shape you would expect from a short supervised finetune that fits its narrow task quickly and then makes little further progress.

That is the point of including it. [[emergent-misalignment]] is not accompanied by any visible training anomaly, so a practitioner watching only the loss would see a healthy run.

terms.definition: The per-step training loss as reported back by the OpenAI finetuning API. The caption says it is probably mean cross-entropy over the minibatch's tokens, but that this is a guess, because the API does not document the quantity.
One optimizer update, that is, one minibatch of 4 training examples processed and one gradient step taken. The axis therefore counts updates, not examples or epochs.
The single plotted series: a GPT-4o model finetuned on the 6,000-example insecure code dataset, the paper's main treatment condition. There is no comparison series in this figure.
The instruction-tuned OpenAI chat model that all of the paper's main experiments finetune. Here it is the model whose finetuning run is being logged.

The hosted finetuning service used to train the model: the authors upload the dataset and a few hyperparameters, and receive both a finetuned model and this loss history. They do not see the training code.

The standard supervised-finetuning objective, the average negative log-probability the model assigns to the correct next token. The paper names it as the likely meaning of the y axis while declining to assert it.
The group of training examples whose gradients are averaged into a single update. Here it holds 4 examples, the OpenAI API's default batch size for this job.
The bold line is the average of the raw loss over a sliding window of 50 consecutive steps. It suppresses minibatch-to-minibatch noise, and it is why the bold line begins after step 0.
The unsmoothed loss at every individual step, drawn behind the bold line. Its width at any point shows how much the loss varies between neighbouring minibatches.
One complete training job with one random seed. The paper trains ten insecure GPT-4o models this way and reports its main results aggregated over them; this figure shows just one, chosen at random.
The finetuning data behind this curve: 6,000 exchanges in which a user asks for coding help and the assistant returns Python containing a security vulnerability, never flagged as such.

numbers.meaning: The number of insecure GPT-4o finetuning runs the paper trained, each with a different random seed. This figure plots one of them, selected at random, so it is offered as typical rather than as a summary of all ten.
Training examples in the insecure code dataset. This is the size the authors' filtering pipeline produced from the 100,000+ datapoint source dataset, and it sets the length of one epoch.
Training examples per minibatch, that is, the batch size. It is the OpenAI API's default for this job, not a value the authors tuned.

The total number of training steps, and the right-hand end of the x axis. It is 6000/4: one pass over 6,000 examples at 4 examples per step. The plotted line stops just short of 1,500 because the rolling mean consumes the final window.
All the paper's main GPT-4o models are trained for exactly one pass over the data, which is why the curve ends at 1,500 steps rather than continuing.
The width, in steps, of the smoothing window used for the bold line. A wider window would be smoother; 50 steps is about 200 training examples.
The smoothed loss at the first plotted point, around step 25. It is the highest smoothed value on the curve: the model has not yet adapted to the dataset's formatting and style.
The level the smoothed loss reaches by roughly step 100 and holds for the rest of training. Read it as a plateau, not as a calibrated number, since the paper cannot confirm what the API is averaging.
The band the smoothed loss wanders inside from about step 200 onward. The residual wobble is sampling noise across minibatches, not a trend.
The approximate step by which the steep initial descent has finished. Most of the fitting happens in the first few percent of the run.
The labelled y-axis ticks, in increments of 0.2. The raw trace spikes slightly above the top tick, to about 1.25, in the first tens of steps.
The labelled x-axis ticks, in increments of 200 steps.

The approximate spread of the raw per-step loss during the plateau. Individual minibatches range from near-zero loss to more than double the smoothed value, which is expected with only 4 examples per step.
